findings: final-layer token states preserve materially more directional relation information than either pooled view
the trained semantic projection does not improve directional role accuracy and compresses opposite-role distance
causes and supports remain at chance even with token-level late interaction
the failure is therefore mixed: pooling/interface loss for some relations plus unresolved upstream semantic weakness for others
architecture_conclusion.next_question: whether directional causes/supports semantics exist in earlier frozen transformer layers and are lost by final-layer shaping

sources: Probing Linguistic Features of Sentence-Level Representations in Neural Relation Extraction
Probing Relational Knowledge in Language Models via Word Analogies
Identifying Linear Relational Concepts in Large Language Models
Do Language Models Encode Semantic Relations? Probing and Sparse Feature Analysis
external_research_basis.conclusion: relation-direction signal can be layer-dependent; inspect frozen layerwise token representations before deciding between a new language-graph interface and semantic retraining

decision_policy.if_mid_layer_restores_causes_supports: design a token-level relation-aware language-to-graph interface tapping the informative frozen layer(s); do not retrain the graph selector against final pooled queries
decision_policy.if_no_layer_restores_causes_supports: stop evidence-graph repair and reopen public semantic representation learning/objectives for directional causal/support semantics

scale_decision.reason: 575801 shows representation/interface localization, not a proven global capacity bottleneck
